status: Authored placement and continuation expectations; parser/lowering/runtime/public unexecuted
rule: W uses one bounded token parenthesis index: only a first opening pair whose matching close reaches the CTAS input end is a Compute wrapper. Other grouped primaries remain Pure. No catalog or type lookup selects the parse branch.

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT 1 AS id |> RESULT before_write)
CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT 1 AS id) |> RESULT before_write
cases.expected_placement: accepted Compute continuation of a Pure grouped primary

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT 1 AS id |> RESULT forbidden) |> WHERE id > 0
cases.expected_placement: refuse RESULT in Pure primary before Program issuance or I/O

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS ((SELECT 1 AS id |> RESULT forbidden))
cases.expected_placement: refuse RESULT in inner Pure primary; outer Compute does not promote it

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT 2 AS id) UNION ALL (SELECT 1 AS id) ORDER BY id
cases.expected_placement: accepted Compute query with Pure set operands
cases.obligation: Retain UNION ALL, both operands and the final ORDER.

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT 1 AS id) |> WHERE id = 2
cases.expected_placement: accepted Compute query with Pure grouped primary

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT 1 AS id |> RESULT before_write |> WHERE id = 2)
cases.obligation: An earlier explicit Result remains a demand root; final write input is the filtered continuation.

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT ')' AS value);
cases.expected_placement: accepted Compute input; quoted close is a string token

cases.source: CREATE TABLE output AS (SELECT 1 AS id /* ) */) |> WHERE id = 2;
cases.expected_placement: accepted Compute continuation; comment close is not a token

cases.source: WITH unused AS (SELECT 1 AS id |> RESULT forbidden) SELECT 2 AS id
cases.expected_placement: refuse RESULT in Pure binding even though unused; zero Run admission and provider I/O

exception: token-string-close exposes value as non-null string bounded by its existing literal contract; no new contract or serializer is introduced
